quotes.text: You can’t retrieve custom payment method types through the API, so store the type ID in your database for use when creating payment methods.
The Express Checkout Element can display custom payment method buttons alongside wallets, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay.
Your platform account can create custom payment methods in its connected accounts using its own custom payment method types, as well as the connected account’s custom payment method types.
Stripe isn’t responsible for the processing of any transactions with any PSP including, for example, any charges, refunds, disputes, settlements, or funds flows.

old_evidence.text: Alternatively, use one of over 50 preset methods for common payment methods processed outside of Stripe.

findings: November product matrix changes Checkout and Express Checkout Element from unsupported to supported, with private preview explicitly attached to Express Checkout Element only. Express Checkout Element has new substantive prose for custom buttons alongside Apple Pay/Google Pay, plus an implementation link. Payment Links remains unsupported, while Connect, Payment Element, Mobile Payment Element, Subscriptions, Invoicing and Customer Portal remain supported.

Dashboard creates branded types, November guides users to presets for Payment Element and custom branding for a custom frontend or Payment Methods API. The type ID is stored by the merchant and cannot be retrieved through the API, while custom PaymentMethod instances can be created and retrieved with type custom and the Dashboard cpmt_ ID in custom[type].

Transaction authorization and processing stay with the merchant and third-party PSP, including charges, refunds, disputes, settlement and completion/reconciliation after selection. Stripe can optionally receive Payment Records for reporting and manage Billing subscription state and tracking of external payments; a record is not Stripe processing.

Connect platform can create the method in a connected account with its own or the connected account’s type. May’s Node stripeAccount option and November’s cURL Stripe-Account header both express connected-account request scope. Existing source describes the option itself as a header.

Compliance retains PSP agreement and regulatory responsibilities, marks rights and no deceptive display, Indonesian/Thai crypto restrictions, and removal/disable obligations upon PSP agreement termination or Stripe prohibition, including Stripe-controlled availability and non-rendering when required removal is ignored.
substantive_changes: Checkout now marked supported at product level in the November matrix; Express Checkout Element changes to private preview and has custom-button display guidance. Do not extend these labels to hosted UI details, preview requirements or live processing behavior absent evidence.

November reorganizes setup, headings, and JSON formatting and swaps Node for cURL without changing the PaymentMethod creation and Connect account scope. The external processor, Payment Records, Billing and compliance boundaries remain supported.
May quantified over 50 presets, whereas November describes presets without a count. Keep the May figure as dated rather than declaring a current count or loss of presets.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 8, 2026 marks Checkout and Express Checkout Element unsupported and lists more than 50 external payment-method presets. Retain the dated baseline alongside November evidence.

Both dates distinguish Dashboard types and API-created method objects, preserve optional external reporting and Connect account scope, and leave payment and downstream disputes/refunds/settlement with the external payment chain.
conflicts: Mapped source lines 32 and 34 still show Checkout and Express Checkout Element unsupported; November’s matrix lists Checkout support and private-preview Express Checkout Element.
Mapped source line 38 calls stripeAccount a header, but May uses it as the SDK option and November shows the separate Stripe-Account HTTP header.

Concept already carries the dated matrix boundaries. Its preset count should be attributed to the May source, and the November overview’s alongside-wallets sentence can support the reciprocal summary without asserting implementation details.
unresolved_questions: The November overview does not establish which Checkout UI variants expose custom payment methods, hosted compatibility, API parity, account preview enrollment or a successful live payment or render.
The November overview does not quantify the current preset catalog or provide the separately linked Express Checkout implementation steps in this page.

findings: Date the May row and incorporate the November product matrix, private-preview scope and explicit custom-button display behavior. Preserve type storage versus PaymentMethod retrieval, quote the May-only preset count with its date and distinguish SDK option from HTTP header.
conflicts: The sole summary preserves May’s obsolete unqualified Checkout and Express Checkout Element rows, and conflates the SDK account option and HTTP header.
source_assessments.reason: The mapped source currently misstates two materially changed product levels. The reciprocal CPM concept already carries the feature/date distinction and can point to the revised evidence.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/custom-payment-methods, source-stripe-custom-payment-methods.md covers a merchant’s Dashboard-created custom payment method type, stored ID, and a PaymentMethod instance created with type custom and custom[type]. Old raw lines 12–44 and new raw lines 13–32 distinguish non-retrievable types from API-managed instances. Old raw lines 76–109 and new raw lines 65–86 let a Connect platform use its own or the connected account’s type in the connected account and retain Stripe Billing tracking for external payments. Old raw lines 131–147 and new raw lines 116–132 put customer flow completion, processing and reconciliation with merchant or PSP and support optional recording in Stripe under new raw lines 7–11. New raw lines 57–71 add Checkout product support and private-preview Express Checkout buttons, while Payment Links stays excluded.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/custom-payment-methods, source-stripe-custom-payment-methods.md should preserve the May unsupported Checkout and Express Checkout Element baseline in old raw lines 68–76 and the November matrix change, Express Checkout private-preview footnote and substantive button-display sentence in new raw lines 57–71. A section link routes to implementation and does not establish hosted UI coverage or live account enablement. Old raw lines 14–27 quantify over 50 presets, while new raw lines 15–25 give branding guidance without a count. The Node-to-cURL and layout changes preserve behavior, with old raw lines 90–111 using the SDK account option and new raw lines 79–87 showing the HTTP header. Keep the existing two-way link with wiki/concepts/stripe-custom-payment-methods.md, add the evidence to the Express Checkout concept’s existing dated preview discussion where relevant, and refresh the source listing in wiki/stripe-index.md.
